raw.abstractText: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent the first line of host immune defense against a broad spectrum of microorganisms. Whether naturally occurring or synthetically designed, these small peptides can potently inhibit microbial growth and remain stable under diverse conditions. Most AMPs act by directly disrupting fungal or bacterial membranes. In this study, we identified a glycine-rich peptide with strong antifungal activity against Botrytis cinerea. We further investigated its mode of action (MOA) and demonstrated its preventive antifungal activity in plants. Our work focuses primarily on the in vitro characterization of AMP features in the context of plant-Botrytis interactions.

raw.abstractText: Virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) is a powerful reverse genetics tool that enables the transient knockdown of gene expression in plants by exploiting their natural antiviral defense mechanisms. This chapter presents a detailed protocol for applying a Cowpea severe mosaic virus (CPSMV)-based VIGS system to study gene function in soybean (Glycine max), with a focus on symbiotic root nodulation. VIGS allows systemic silencing of target genes, making it especially valuable to study pathways involving systemic signaling. The protocol includes Agrobacterium-mediated propagation of CPSMV variants in Nicotiana benthamiana, followed by mechanical inoculation of soybean plants and nodulation analysis. Detailed steps for vector construction, viral amplification, plant infection, and downstream molecular and phenotypic analyses are provided. This protocol is reproducible, accessible, and suitable for functional genomics studies in soybean, particularly for genes involved in nodulation but also in other developmental or stress-related processes.

raw.abstractText: This study aimed to explore the processing mechanism of single medicinal herbs in compound prescriptions, compare the pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic changes of Yuanhu Zhitong Formula before and after processing, and elucidate its underlying mechanism against gastric ulcers. The results showed that six components, namely, corydaline, coptisine chloride, palmatine, berberine chloride, phellopterin, and imperatorin, exerted anti-ulcer activities. The optimal vinegar-processing parameters for Corydalis yanhusuo were determined as follows: processing temperature of 84°C, vinegar dosage of 37%, and baking time of 35 min. Vinegar-processed Corydalis yanhusuo could accelerate the in vivo distribution of alkaloid components in the formula, elevate the plasma concentration, and prolong the in vivo retention time of coumarin components. The synergistic effects of the two types of active ingredients endow the vinegar-processed Yuanhu Zhitong Formula with significantly superior antigastric ulcer activity compared with the raw formula. Moreover, network pharmacology results revealed that this formula exerts therapeutic effects against gastric ulcers mainly by regulating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. This study clarified the optimal processing technology and the pharmacodynamic material basis of Yuanhu Zhitong Formula against gastric ulcers, confirmed the efficacy-enhancing effect of processing, and provided data support for the formulation of its processing production standards and clinical medication.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Caffeine is consumed for its presumed cognitive benefits, yet controlled studies have repeatedly failed to find effects on inhibitory control. Cross-sectional work suggests that people with elevated attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms may benefit from chronic, moderate caffeine consumption, but whether acute intake improves cognition in proportion to symptom severity has not been tested experimentally.

Aims

We tested whether 250 mg of caffeine improves active inhibition (withholding a prepared response) and reactive inhibition (resolving response conflict), and whether ADHD symptom severity moderates these effects.

Methods

In a preregistered, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial, a nonclinical sample of 36 young adults received 250 mg of caffeine or placebo in counterbalanced order, with testing 45 min after ingestion. Active inhibition was assessed with a Go/No-Go task (204 trials), reactive inhibition with an arrow flanker task (200 trials) and symptoms with the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale. Mixed-effects models included treatment, symptom severity, their interaction and ten covariates; Bayes factors quantified evidence for the null.

Results

Both tasks produced their benchmark effects (dz = 1.24 and 1.09) and all indices were reliable (split-half r = 0.73-0.98). Caffeine affected neither commission errors (BF01 = 4.98), response criterion (5.14), Go reaction time (2.83), reaction time variability (4.35), flanker reaction time (5.49) nor flanker accuracy (5.09). ADHD symptoms moderated no effect (15 preregistered tests; smallest p = 0.514), yet predicted performance itself (flanker accuracy r = -0.42), indicating that the null is not due to an insensitive measure.

Conclusions

Caffeine produced no acute benefit for either form of inhibition, and ADHD symptoms did not moderate its effects. Bayes factors supported the absence rather than the nondetection of these effects, arguing against an acute improvement of inhibitory control that scales with ADHD symptom severity in nonclinical young adults. Whether this also holds for chronic consumption or for adults with diagnosed ADHD remains to be tested.

raw.abstractText:
Objective

Caffeine could improve cognitive functions, but study protocols usually prohibit drinking coffee before cognitive testing. However, regular coffee consumers may experience withdrawal effects when they cannot drink their habitual coffee, which may impair cognitive performance. Therefore, we tested the effects of overnight coffee abstinence in regular coffee consumers: once allowing to drink their coffee and once not drinking coffee. The cognitive performance was compared with non-regular coffee consumers.

Methods

Thirty regular coffee consumers (RCCs) and 25 non-regular consumers (N-RCCs) took part in this study. RCCs were tested after their habitual morning coffee (c-RCC) and after overnight abstinence (a-RCC); N-RCCs were tested once. A cognitive battery assessed reaction time (RT), processing speed (digit symbol substitution test), working memory, verbal learning/memory and executive function (Stroop). Sleep quality was included as a covariate.

Results

Compared to c-RCC, overnight coffee abstinence significantly slowed RTs but did not affect the performance in the other cognitive tasks. In the a-RCC condition, but not the c-RCC condition, the RTs were slower than those of the N-RCCs, while accuracy measures were comparable across groups. Sleep quality did not alter these findings.

Conclusions

Overnight coffee abstinence selectively slowed RT, and no statistical support was found for effects on memory or executive function. This suggests that overnight coffee abstinence protocols may introduce withdrawal-related RT slowing as a confound in habitual consumers, whereas other cognitive domains may not be affected. Allowing habitual consumers to maintain normal coffee intake could reduce this bias, supporting tailored rather than uniform abstinence requirements based on the specific outcomes studied.

raw.abstractText: The collagen triple helix is the most abundant protein structural motif in animals. It tolerates any amino acid in its Xaa and Yaa positions but demands glycine (Gly) at every third position, where the residue packs into the sterically forbidding core of the triple helix and donates the recurring interstrand N-H⋯OC hydrogen bond that stitches the three strands together. (2S)-Proline (Pro) and (2S,4R)-4-hydroxyproline (Hyp) are enriched far above their proteome-wide abundance because they preorganize individual strands into the polyproline II conformation, lowering the entropic cost of folding. We asked whether the triple helix is intrinsically stable enough to form from strands that carry no such preorganization, that is, from polyglycine. To offset the conformational entropy of a Gly-rich tract, we embedded Gly<sub>6</sub> within flanking triple-helical (Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>n</sub> clamps in Ac-(Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>6</sub>-Gly<sub>6</sub>-(Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>5</sub>-Pro-Hyp-NH<sub>2</sub> and compared it with an otherwise identical peptide in which Gly<sub>6</sub> was replaced by two [2-(2-aminoethoxy)ethoxy]acetic acid units, a flexible, length-matched spacer that lacks most of the regularly spaced backbone amides of Gly<sub>6</sub>. Circular dichroism spectroscopy revealed the diagnostic positive band at 225 nm. The molar ellipticity of the spacer-containing control was 86% of that of the Gly<sub>6</sub>-containing peptide, matching the 35/41 = 85% ratio of residues capable of triple-helix formation and consistent with the Gly<sub>6</sub> segment contributing to the triple-helical signal. Thermal denaturation yielded a T<sub>m</sub> of 46.8°C for the Gly<sub>6</sub>-containing peptide, 6.3°C higher than that of the matched spacer control. This added stability indicates that the polyglycine tract is not merely accommodated within the helix but contributes stabilizing interstrand hydrogen bonds. Together, these data indicate that three polyglycine strands can form a collagen triple helix when flanked by triple-helical clamps. This result is consistent with the idea that the triple-helical architecture predates the recruitment of Pro and Hyp, informs the evolutionary origin of collagen, and offers a blunt-ended, symmetric scaffold for designing peptidic triple helices.

raw.abstractText:
While insulin activates the sympathetic nervous system in experimental settings, whether therapeutic insulin administration is associated with cardiac sympathetic predominance under free-living conditions remains unclear. This prospective observational study investigated the association between insulin dosing and cardiac autonomic balance in adults with type 1 diabetes managed exclusively with insulin therapy. Participants underwent continuous heart rate variability (HRV) and glucose monitoring over 4 consecutive days during routine daily activities. Cardiac sympathetic predominance was assessed using the low-frequency power to high-frequency power (LF/HF) ratio derived from HRV analysis, and associations were evaluated using generalized estimating equations. A higher last bolus insulin dose was associated with an increased LF/HF ratio during the early sleep phase. A higher basal insulin dose was also associated with an increased LF/HF ratio during the late sleep phase. These associations persisted after adjustment for mean glucose and mean absolute glucose change during the corresponding sleep phases. Under free-living conditions, higher insulin doses were associated with dose-dependent increases in cardiac sympathetic predominance, independent of glycemic profiles. These findings suggest that insulin dosing may be linked to cardiac autonomic regulation in individuals with type 1 diabetes, highlighting the importance of considering cardiac autonomic balance and potential cardiovascular risk when optimizing insulin therapy.

Article highlights

The relationship between therapeutic insulin administration and cardiac autonomic balance under free-living conditions remains unclear. We examined whether insulin dosing was associated with cardiac sympathetic predominance during daily life in adults with type 1 diabetes managed with insulin therapy. Higher last bolus and basal insulin doses were associated with increased cardiac sympathetic predominance during the early and late sleep phases, respectively, independent of glycemic profiles. These findings suggest that insulin dosing patterns may be linked to cardiac autonomic balance, with potential implications for optimizing insulin therapy in type 1 diabetes.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Prolonged exposure to hepatotoxic antiretroviral therapy (ART) could lead to chronic liver injury, which might increase risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We used causal inference methods to evaluate if cumulative exposure to ART with known mechanisms of chronic liver injury is associated with HCC among people with HIV (PWH), by chronic liver disease (CLD) status.

Methods

We conducted a cohort study of antiretroviral-naive PWH with and without diagnosed CLD who initiated ART in the Veterans Affairs between 1999 and 2023. Exposure to ART with known mechanism of chronic liver injury (mitochondrial toxicity or accumulation of toxic intermediates) was determined monthly through prescription fills. Incident HCC was identified by Veterans Affairs National Cancer Registry and/or recorded diagnoses. Marginal structural models estimated odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of HCC associated with cumulative exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART compared with ART without chronic liver injury mechanisms, by CLD status.

Results

Among 11,854 PWH without CLD and 6771 PWH with CLD, we observed 112 and 378 HCC events, respectively. Among PWH without CLD, ≥4 years of exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART was associated with HCC when compared with ≥4 years of use of ART without chronic liver injury mechanisms (OR = 4.02 [95% CI: 1.00-16.24]). Among PWH with CLD, ≥4 years of exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART was not associated with HCC (OR = 1.36; 95% CI: 0.68-2.72).

Conclusion

Four or more years of ART with a chronic liver injury mechanism was associated with HCC among PWH without CLD, but not those with CLD.

raw.abstractText: Melatonin (MEL) is an endogenous hormone that regulates circadian rhythm, immune function and oxidative stress responses. Norepinephrine (NE), an endogenous catecholamine, increases blood pressure through the sympathetic nervous system and is commonly administered intraoperatively or in the clinically ill patient for hemodynamic support. Although endogenous NE is known to stimulate MEL synthesis, the effects of exogenous intravenous NE on plasma MEL concentration, particularly under general anaesthesia (GA), remain poorly characterised. This study examined the influence of intravenous NE on plasma MEL concentrations in healthy volunteers, both awake and under general anaesthesia. A secondary analysis was conducted using data from a prospective, single-centre, cross-over study involving volunteers who received stepwise NE infusions while awake and under total intravenous general anaesthesia. Arterial blood samples were collected to determine plasma MEL and NE concentrations. Linear mixed-effects modelling was used to assess the relationship between NE and MEL concentrations. A total of 36 healthy volunteers were enroled, yielding 417 MEL-NE samples. Intravenous NE administration was significantly associated with higher plasma MEL concentration, corresponding to an estimated 26% increase in MEL per 1 standard-deviation increase in NE concentration (Estimate = 0.230, p < 0.001). MEL concentrations were approximately 43% higher in the awake phase compared to GA (Estimate = 0.356, p < 0.001). GA did not significantly modify the NE-MEL association (Estimate = -0.02877, p = 0.528). Substantial positive correlation was observed between baseline MEL concentrations and the magnitude of the response to NE administration (r = 0.74). In conclusion, intravenous NE increases plasma MEL concentrations in both awake and anaesthetised individuals. Substantial interindividual variation in MEL response suggests underlying physiological differences. Future studies should explore the long-term effects of NE administration on MEL concentrations. raw.abstractText:
Background

Sleep deprivation and poor sleep quality are critical problems among intensive care unit (ICU) patients, with significant implications for recovery, delirium onset and clinical outcomes. Despite growing scientific interest, no bibliometric study has systematically mapped the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of this field.

Aim

To analyse the bibliometric characteristics and thematic structure of publications on sleep deprivation, sleep promotion and sleep quality in ICU patients indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) database between 1983 and 2026.

Study design

A descriptive and evaluative bibliometric analysis was conducted. Data were retrieved on April 26, 2026, from the WoS Core Collection using a comprehensive search strategy. Publications were filtered by document type, WoS categories (nursing, critical care medicine, anaesthesiology) and index (SCI-EXPANDED, SSCI, ESCI). Data were analysed using R software with the Biblioshiny interface, and annual publication trends were evaluated using Microsoft Excel.

Results

Of 11 418 publications retrieved, 379 met the inclusion criteria, spanning 37 years (1983-2026). Linear regression revealed a statistically significant positive trend in publication output (β = 0.643, R2 = 0.704, r = 0.839, p < 0.001), with mean annual publications of 10.24 ± 8.83 and notable acceleration from the 2000s onwards. Thematic mapping identified 'sleep', 'sleep deprivation' and 'delirium' as motor themes both highly central and well developed. Emerging concepts included circadian rhythm, actigraphy, fatigue, pain and anxiety.

Conclusions

ICU sleep research has grown substantially over four decades, with sleep deprivation and delirium emerging as co-dominant research priorities. Thematic gaps and emerging clusters identified in this analysis highlight important directions for future nursing research and evidence-based practice development in critical care.

Relevance to clinical practice

This bibliometric analysis identified sleep deprivation and delirium as the co-dominant motor themes of ICU sleep research, and intervention-related concepts such as earplugs, eye masks and melatonin as emerging clusters. These evidence-based trends can guide ICU nurses in prioritizing targeted sleep promotion protocols and support policymakers in directing resources toward the most scientifically mature intervention areas in critical care.

Objective

To compare serum total tau and α-synuclein among controls, drug-naïve children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and children with ADHD receiving methylphenidate.

Original ELISA spreadsheets provided 26 controls, 29 evaluable drug-naïve participants and 32 methylphenidate-treated participants. Results

α-Synuclein differed among groups (H = 49.859, p < 0.001, ε2 = 0.570), with all pairwise contrasts significant. Conclusions

Serum α-synuclein and total tau showed distinct cross-sectional group patterns. These associations do not establish methylphenidate effects and require prospective confirmation.

raw.abstractText: TYRO3, AXL, and MERTK, the TAM receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), play roles in phagocytosis and negative regulation of immune responses, contributing to homeostasis in many adult tissues. Aberrant TAM signaling leads to diseases including autoimmune disorders, viral infection, inflammation, and cancer. Development of successful drugs targeting TAM receptors is hindered by incomplete knowledge of the receptor activation mechanism. Receptor dimerization is assumed to play a role, as seen for most RTKs. However, full biological responses require the TAM ligands to engage phosphatidylserine in an opposing cell or virus membrane, suggesting a more complex mechanism, possibly involving higher-order receptor oligomerization or clustering. Here, we present an X-ray crystal structure of the ectodomain of MERTK, which adopts a highly curved conformation with key interdomain boundaries stabilized by N-linked glycan moieties. We show that this MERTK extracellular region (ECR) forms a similar conformation in solution using small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), which also suggests a flexible ECR. We compare these crystallographic and solution data for MERTK with SAXS and AlphaFold structural predictions for the other two TAM receptors. SAXS data confirm that each TAM ECR has a distinct curvature, with TYRO3 the most bent and AXL relatively straight. This leads us to speculate that these different ectodomain conformations guide receptor-specific functions. The MERTK X-ray crystal structure also suggests a head-to-tail intermolecular interaction between the Ig2 domain of one MERTK and the FNIIIb domain of a second that has intriguing parallels with interactions that have been proposed to regulate Eph receptor clustering.

raw.abstractText: Activity-guided separation of medicinal plants requires linking activity signals and chromatographic resolution in complex matrices. In this study, based on a previously established HPLC-DPPH platform, medium-pressure prefractionation and preparative chromatographic purification were applied for the targeted isolation of free radical scavengers from Saxifraga tangutica (S. tangutica). Medium-pressure prefractionation reduced sample complexity and enriched active fractions, while Click XION chromatography concentrated the target fraction. Subsequent purification on the ReproSil-Pur C18 AQ column resolved this fraction into two baseline-separated active peaks, affording compounds with purities greater than 95%. The isolated compounds were identified as quercetin-3-O-β-D-glucoside-7-O-β-D-glucoside and quercetin-3-O-β-D-galactoside-7-O-β-D-glucoside, a pair of C-4″-epimeric quercetin 3,7-di-O-glycosides. Both compounds exhibited DPPH radical-scavenging activity, with IC<sub>50</sub> values of 68.94 ± 2.77 and 75.59 ± 2.14 μM, respectively. DFT calculations, molecular docking, and ADMET prediction further supported the comparative interpretation of their electronic features, antioxidant-related interaction potential, and predicted pharmacokinetic profiles. Overall, this study achieved the activity guided isolation and activity evaluation of a pair of high-purity C-4″-epimeric flavonol diglycosides from S. tangutica, providing a practical chromatographic strategy for the targeted characterization of structurally similar bioactive constituents from medicinal plants.

raw.abstractText: Vitamin D is a nutrient and prohormone obtained from diet and supplements and synthesized in the skin. It is essential for calcium and phosphate homeostasis and skeletal health and influences multiple extra-skeletal processes, yet deficiency remains common worldwide. This narrative review summarizes vitamin D sources, physiology, metabolism, pharmacokinetics, clinical relevance and safety and outlines the distinct pharmacokinetic profiles and clinical roles of vitamin D, calcidiol and calcitriol and its analogues. Evidence consistently supports vitamin D, combined with calcium, for preventing and treating deficiency-related skeletal disorders in high-risk populations, and in specific conditions such as malabsorption, chronic kidney disease, hypoparathyroidism and frailty. In vitamin D-replete populations, large trials show limited extra-skeletal benefits, apart from modest effects on cancer mortality and progression from prediabetes to Type 2 diabetes. Untargeted screening is not recommended. Future research should prioritize targeted supplementation, standardized assays and identification of populations most likely to benefit from supplementation.

raw.abstractText: Cellular immunotherapies have transformed oncologic treatment in recent years, yet the inability to monitor cell migration post-transfusion remains a significant barrier to their development. Here, we explore the feasibility of a non-invasive cell-tracking method utilizing Cu(I)-catalyzed click chemistry in which cells are first labeled with alkynes and, after 1-2 weeks, are selectively targeted via an azide-conjugated fluorescent probe. We developed Click1, a novel tris-Cu-chelating azide capable of a rapid, robust click reaction directly on live cell surfaces with minimal cytotoxicity. When paired with Click1, two distinct alkyne-labeling reagents, N-(4-pentynoyl)-mannosamine-tetraacylated (Ac4ManNAl) and propargyl choline, were capable of detecting human T cells for over two weeks. Our findings elucidate the metabolic turnover of biochemical handles in primary immune cells, providing a potential framework for long-term cell tracking in immunotherapies.

raw.abstractText: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is an important and significant reason for cancer-related morbidity and mortality globally. Treatment remains challenging due to recurrence, metastasis, and chemoresistance. Evidence shows that oxidative stress, ongoing inflammation, and cancer stem cells (CSCs) play essential functions in CRC development and progression. Nrf2 is a master regulator of cellular redox balance through the Keap1-Nrf2-is signalling pathway. Normal activation of Nrf2 protects colonic cells from oxidative DNA harm and inflammation during initial carcinogenesis. However, sustained Nrf2 activation in tumours encourages chemoresistance, metabolic reprogramming, and CSC upkeep, showing a dual role. Traditional medicine and dietary phytochemicals (curcumin, sulforaphane, resveratrol, EGCG, berberine) can modulate Nrf2 while interacting with NF-κB, Wnt/β-catenin, and Notch pathways. This review synthesises mechanistic and translational evidence on Nrf2 modulation in CRC chemoprevention, stressing conventional medicine-derived agents in modern approaches. It moreover highlights difficulties, limitations, and future viewpoints for precision chemoprevention and personalised interventions.

raw.abstractText:
Background:

Liver diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) often shows signal loss in the left lobe due to cardiac pulsation, known as the pulsation artifact.

Purpose:

This study was conducted to turn this bug into a feature. We hypothesized that the pulsation artifact, caused by mechanically transmitted waves, is influenced by tissue stiffness and, thereby, indicative of cirrhosis in the left liver lobe. Thus, we evaluated the potential of DWI pulsation artifacts to detect liver cirrhosis. Study type: This study included both retrospective patients and prospective healthy volunteers. Study population: Thirteen healthy volunteers, 16 patients with cirrhosis (Ishak 5 or 6), and three patients without cirrhosis (Ishak 0, 1, or 2) were included. Field Strength/Sequence: Imaging was performed at 1.5 T and 3 T using echoplanar DWI of the liver with two b-values, b50 = 50 s/mm2 and b800 = 800 s/mm2. Assessment: After manual segmentation of the left and right liver lobes, 18 first-order features were extracted from b50 and b800 images. We assumed the pulsation artifact was predominantly present in the left liver lobe in the b800 images. Thus, we computed the ratios of the intensity-normalized b800 features obtained from the left and right liver lobes. Additionally, we performed an intensity normalization to address the sometimes different signal intensities of left and right liver lobe. Then, we conducted a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis to differentiate cirrhotic from non- cirrhotic livers. Statistical tests: ROC analysis and leave-one-out bootstrapping were applied, both yielding area under the curve (AUC) values.

Results:

Left liver pulsation artifacts were more pronounced in non-cirrhotic livers and largely absent in cirrhotic livers. The first quartile feature, i.e. the first quartile of the normalized signal, best distinguished cirrhotic from non-cirrhotic livers (AUC = 0.95; 95% confidence interval 0.87–1.00). Data conclusion: The left liver DWI pulsation artifact reflects liver stiffness and could serve as a simple, intrinsic marker of liver cirrhosis. Analysis of the signal magnitude can differentiate cirrhotic from non-cirrhotic livers.

raw.abstractText:
Background:

Dichlorvos is a widely used organophosphate pesticide associated with neurotoxicity through acetylcholinesterase inhibition, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation. Chronic exposure may cause neuronal dysfunction and structural brain alterations. Ascorbic acid (vitamin C), a potent antioxidant, may provide neuroprotection against oxidative damage. This study evaluated the protective effects of ascorbic acid against dichlorvos—induced neurobehavioral and oxido—inflammatory alterations in adult male Wistar rats.

Methods:

Thirty—six rats were randomly assigned into six groups (n = 6): control, dichlorvos (20 mg/kg), dichlorvos plus low—dose ascorbic acid (50 mg/kg), low—dose ascorbic acid, dichlorvos plus high-dose ascorbic acid (150 mg/kg), and high—dose ascorbic acid groups. Treatments were administered orally for six weeks. Neurobehavioral performance was assessed using the T—maze and hanging—wire tests. Oxidative stress biomarkers, including malondialdehyde, superoxide dismutase, and catalase, were evaluated in the hippocampus and amygdala. Histological examinations of the hippocampus, cerebellum, and prefrontal cortex were also performed. Data were analyzed using one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc test ().

Results:

No significant difference in brain weight was observed across groups. Neurobehavioral assessments showed no statistically significant differences between pre— and post—treatment performances, although dichlorvos exposure produced a slight decline, while ascorbic acid—treated groups showed dose—dependent improvement. Dichlorvos significantly increased malondialdehyde levels and decreased superoxide dismutase and catalase activities compared with control (p < 0.05). Co—administration of ascorbic acid significantly reduced lipid peroxidation and improved antioxidant enzyme activities relative to the dichlorvos group (p <0.05). Histologically, the hippocampus remained largely preserved, while mild neuronal degeneration was observed in the prefrontal cortex of dichlorvos—treated rats. The cerebellum showed mostly normal architecture, with mild molecular layer degeneration in the high—dose dichlorvos plus ascorbic acid group.

Conclusions:

Ascorbic acid attenuated dichlorvos—induced oxidative stress and reduced associated histopathological alterations, with limited but observable improvements in neurobehavioral outcomes. These findings suggest its potential protective role against organophosphate—induced neurotoxicity.

raw.abstractText: Long-term intensive fertilization has accumulated large legacy phosphorus (P) pools in greenhouse vegetable soils, while substituting chemical fertilizers with livestock manure may exacerbate soil P loading. We evaluated pakchoi growth and legacy P utilization in an acidified, P-enriched greenhouse soil, comparing an unfertilized, unamended control (CK) with equal-carbon inputs of low-C:P, high-P chicken manure (OF) and high-C:P, low-P plant-derived amendments: alkali lignin (AL), straw (ST), and alkali-lignin-modified straw (AST). Compared with the OF, shoot dry weight was 47.0% and 12.4% higher under ST and AST, respectively, while shoot P uptake increased by 80.2% and 76.8%. OF produced an apparent P surplus, whereas ST and AST generated negative apparent P balances, indicating current-season amendment P inputs could not offset shoot P removal and supporting enhanced legacy P utilization without further accumulation of available or labile inorganic P. Plant-derived amendments increased soil C:P and pH, generally enhanced C- and N-acquiring enzyme activities, and reduced ecoenzymatic vector angles, alleviating relative microbial P-acquisition limitation. raw.abstractText: Background Cell therapy is a promising approach for treating neurological disorders, but its safety remains a major concern, including the origin of cells, cultivation methods, and route of administration. Repeated systemic delivery is often required for long-term studies, yet the safety of chronic retro-orbital administration of human glial progenitor cells (GPCs) has not been characterised. This pilot study evaluated the potential risks and pathological processes associated with chronic retro-orbital administration of human iPSC-derived GPCs in mice. Methods GPCs were derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells and injected into the retro-orbital venous sinus of male C57Bl/6 J mice under isoflurane anaesthesia. Two pilot experiments were performed: a high-dose experiment with 500 × 10  3 (n = 9), 150 × 10  3 (n = 5), and 50 × 10  3 (n = 5) cells/mouse administered weekly for two months, and a control group (n = 9) receiving dPBS. Locomotor and exploratory activity were assessed in the open field test. Blood biochemical markers (ALT, AST, AST/ALT ratio, LDH, GGT, and total bilirubin) were measured, and brain sections were analysed by H&E staining and immunohistochemistry for glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). Statistical analysis was performed using ANOVA on ranks with Dunn’s post-hoc test or one-way ANOVA with Holm–Sidak correction. Results Chronic administration of the high dose (500 × 10  3 cells/mouse) for 60 days induced a statistically significant increase in ALT, AST, LDH, and total bilirubin levels, and increased the number of GFAP-positive astrocytes in the cerebral cortex (p = 0.046) compared with the control group. In contrast, lower doses (50 × 10  3 and 150 × 10  3 cells/mouse) did not cause elevated blood markers or astrogliosis. No significant changes in locomotor or exploratory behaviour were observed in the open field test, and no pathomorphological changes were detected in the brain in any group. Conclusions Chronic retro-orbital administration of GPCs at 500 × 10  3 cells/mouse was associated with signs of inflammation and liver damage, whereas doses of 50 × 10  3 and 150 × 10  3 cells/mouse were safe and optimal. These findings provide important pharmacological parameters for designing preclinical studies using long-term GPC administration in mice.

raw.abstractText: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) exhibits profound clinical heterogeneity; however, its underlying neurobiological substrates remain unclear. Here, leveraging large – scale structural magnetic resonance imaging data from 12,663 typically developing children and 1,699 children with ADHD across Chinese and United States cohorts, we construct population specific pediatric brain charts via hierarchical Bayesian normative modeling to quantify individual deviations in cortical morphology. Data-driven clustering identifies two robust, cross – ethnically replicable ADHD biotypes: an infra – normal biotype characterized by widespread cortical thinning and a supra – normal biotype marked by cortical thickening. Multivariate analyses reveal distinct brain–behavior architectures: cortical deviations correlate preferentially with symptom severity in the infra–normal biotype but with both symptom severity and cognitive performance in the supranormal biotype. Clinically, the infra–normal biotype demonstrates a superior response to methylphenidate over atomoxetine, whereas the supra–normal biotype responds comparably to both. Transcriptomic analyses identify biotype–specific molecular signatures converging with ADHD genome–wide association study (GWAS) risk loci but exhibiting distinct expression patterns in the brain. These findings classify ADHD heterogeneity into neurobiologically distinct, clinically informed biotypes, providing a mechanistic framework for precision psychiatry in pediatric ADHD.

raw.abstractText:
Introduction and aim

Epilepsy affects approximately 50 million people worldwide, and a substantial proportion of patients have drug-resistant disease or experience adverse effects from anticonvulsant medications. Berberine, a blood-brain-barrier-permeant isoquinoline alkaloid, has shown anticonvulsant potential in preclinical models. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the preclinical evidence on berberine's anticonvulsant efficacy, its dose-response and formulation dependence, and its mechanisms of action.

Methodology

PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library were searched and reported per PRISMA 2020 (PROSPERO CRD420251135006). Random-effects models (DerSimonian-Laird with Hartung-Knapp adjustment) pooled dichotomous outcomes as risk ratios (RR) and continuous outcomes as standardised mean differences (SMD); pre-specified subgroup, dose-response, leave-one-out and GRADE analyses were conducted.

Results

Sixteen studies were included. Berberine reduced the incidence of status epilepticus/generalised seizure (RR 0.73, 95% CI 0.61-0.87; I2 = 35%), the proportion reaching the fully kindled state (RR 0.53, 0.37-0.75; I2 = 0%) and seizure-related mortality (RR 0.72, 0.60-0.85; I2 = 0%), with a trend toward fewer spontaneous recurrent seizures (RR 0.65, 0.40-1.04). Seizure severity decreased (SMD 3.09, 1.45-4.74) and latency increased (SMD 1.50, 0.23-2.76). A monotonic dose-response gradient was observed across ascending dose tiers (≤25, 50 and ≥ 100 mg/kg; RR 0.88 → 0.67 → 0.41), and nano-encapsulated berberine markedly outperformed conventional berberine (kindling RR 0.04 vs 0.53). Mechanistically, berberine reduced lipid peroxidation (MDA, SMD 1.82, 0.63-3.01) and raised the antioxidant enzyme superoxide dismutase (SOD, SMD 1.44, 0.48-2.40).

Conclusion

Berberine exerts a consistent, dose-dependent, multi-target anticonvulsant effect that is greatly enhanced by nanoformulation. Certainty was moderate for the primary outcome and low-moderate elsewhere, defining berberine as a rational candidate for further translational development in epilepsy.

raw.abstractText: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent chronic liver disorder, with its progressive form, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), characterized by steatosis, inflammation, hepatocyte injury, and fibrosis. However, the underlying mechanism remains incompletely understood. SETDB1 emerged as a key modulator: hepatocyte-specific loss of Setdb1 exacerbated steatosis, inflammation, ductular reaction, and fibrosis, whereas Setdb1 overexpression markedly alleviated these pathological features. Notably, human liver samples showed decreased SETDB1 expression with advancing MASLD. Furthermore, SETDB1 deficiency increased hepatic ferroptosis by upregulating ACSL4, aggravating MASH pathology, whereas ACSL4 knockout reduced liver injury in the absence of SETDB1. SETDB1 overexpression protected against liver damage by repressing ACSL4. Therefore, the SETDB1-ACSL4-ferroptosis axis regulates MASH progression and represents a potential therapeutic target.

raw.abstractText: Polysubstance use is a major contributor to neurotoxicity, yet the integrated redox-dependent mechanisms underlying polydrug exposure remain poorly understood. Cocaine (Coc), nicotine (Nic), and alcohol (Alc) are commonly co-abused substances associated with oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuronal impairment. Here, we investigated the effects of Coc, Nic, Alc, Nic+Alc, and Coc+Nic+Alc exposure on redox homeostasis, mitochondrial function, and epigenetic regulation in mice brain and human microglial cells (HMC3). Individual and polydrug exposures increased reactive oxygen species, altered mitochondrial and antioxidant defense pathways, including GSS, SOD2, PGC-1α, TFAM, and Trx/TXNIP signaling. Polydrug exposure further reduced oxidative phosphorylation complexes, altered NRF1/NRF2-mediated mitochondrial pathways, and decreased Mfn1/2 expression in mice brain tissue, consistent with impaired mitochondrial function and fusion. In HMC3 cells, polysubstance exposure similarly increased oxidative stress, as demonstrated by MitoSOX, DHE, and DCFH-DA assays. These redox and mitochondrial alterations were accompanied by changes in DNMT and TET enzymes, consistent with altered epigenetic regulation. Behaviorally, both individual and polydrug exposures produced significant conditioned place preference. Notably, polydrug exposure was associated with reduced tyrosine hydroxylase immunoreactivity in the substantia nigra, along with altered dopamine transporter and dopamine D2 receptor expression, increased caspase-3 activation and ASC expression, and changes in microglial P2RY12 expression, together with enhanced neuroinflammatory responses. Collectively, these findings identify interconnected redox, mitochondrial, and epigenetic alterations associated with polysubstance-induced neuroadaptation and neurotoxicity. Although selected molecular pathways exhibited partial counter-regulation, persistent mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroinflammatory responses, and alterations in dopaminergic markers were observed following polysubstance exposure, highlighting potential therapeutic targets for substance use disorders.

raw.abstractText: Creatine is among the most extensively studied and widely used nutritional supplements in sports and exercise science. Over the past two decades, however, interest has expanded well beyond skeletal muscle, driven by growing recognition of the central role played by the creatine-phosphocreatine system in cerebral bioenergetics. Experimental evidence indicates that creatine contributes to neuronal energy homeostasis, mitochondrial function, membrane stability and potentially neuroprotection. This has fuelled growing enthusiasm for the idea that creatine supplementation might enhance cognitive function and benefit individuals with compromised cerebral metabolism. Yet, despite strong physiological plausibility, clinical findings remain inconsistent and often difficult to interpret. In this review, it is argued that the gap between proposed mechanisms and available clinical evidence reflects two distinct challenges: biological constraints on cerebral creatine availability after supplementation, and persistent methodological weaknesses in the clinical literature. We contend that the central challenge for the coming decade is not to identify new mechanisms of creatine action in the brain, but to establish, unequivocally, whether measurable changes in cerebral bioenergetics translate into meaningful cognitive benefit - whether as enhanced performance in healthy individuals or as clinically significant improvement in patient populations.

raw.abstractText: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex, progressive neurodegenerative disorder in which amyloid-β accumulation, tau dysregulation, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, synaptic loss and neurodegeneration interact to drive memory loss and cognitive decline. Despite advances in symptomatic therapies and anti-amyloid agents, clinical benefit remains modest, supporting interest in polypharmacological approaches. Cannabidiol (CBD) is a non-psychotropic phytocannabinoid that interacts with several signalling systems relevant to AD, including cannabinoid-related pathways, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ (PPARγ), transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) channels, 5-HT1A signalling, fatty acid-binding proteins involved in anandamide transport, GPR55 and adenosine transporters. The most consistent preclinical findings indicate that CBD attenuates neuroinflammatory and oxidative responses and improves selected behavioural outcomes. Evidence for amyloid-related effects is supportive but heterogeneous. Direct evidence for tau modulation has expanded in transgenic and chemically induced models, but findings remain model-dependent, whereas mitochondrial rescue and adult hippocampal neurogenesis are less firmly established. Methodological variability in CBD source, formulation, dose, route, treatment window, sex, age and outcome selection limits direct comparison between studies. Work on other cannabinoids and CBD:Δ9-THC combinations is discussed for context, and current evidence does not establish CBD as a disease-modifying treatment in AD. Overall, current preclinical evidence supports continued investigation of CBD as a multi-target neuroprotective candidate in AD, provided that future studies use standardized, mechanism-focused and translationally relevant designs. This review compares preclinical evidence across pathological domains and identifies translational research priorities.

raw.abstractText: To explore the feasibility of using coal gasification slag (CGS) as a substitute for limestone filler (LF) in asphalt mastic, six representative CGS powders and one commonly used LF were selected. The physicochemical properties of the CGS powders and the rheological properties of the corresponding asphalt mastics were investigated, and an economic evaluation was conducted. Through comparative analysis of the high- and low-temperature rheological properties of the asphalt mastics at a fixed filler-to-binder (F/B) ratio of 1.0 by mass, low-carbon gasification slag generated by the pulverized-coal process (coded as LCPGS) was identified as the preferred raw material, achieving the optimal balance between high- and low-temperature properties. Compared with LF asphalt mastic, LCPGS asphalt mastic (LCPGS-AM) showed a 19.4% higher G*/sinδ at 64 °C, while m/S value at −12 °C was only 2.2% lower. Based on the rheological and fatigue-resistance properties of LCPGS-AMs with different F/B ratios, a suitable F/B range of 30%–40% by volume was determined, which can serve as a reference for asphalt mastic and mixture design. Complete replacement of conventional LF with LCPGS can reduce material cost by approximately 56.3%, yielding significant economic benefits. The preliminary performance and economic analyses indicate that the use of CGS powder as an alternative filler in asphalt mixtures is feasible.

Together, these findings uncover the signaling basis of sustained psychedelic efficacy and provide a rational framework for developing nonhallucinogenic psychedelic therapies for psychiatric disorders.

raw.abstractText: Digital logistics can improve visibility, coordination, reliability, and customer interaction, yet technological sophistication alone does not guarantee that firms realize these benefits. This study identifies conditions that are necessary and alternative configurations that are sufficient for high perceived e-logistics effectiveness in Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) sector. A cross-sectional survey used random respondent selection, 70 professionals were invited and 60 usable questionnaires were returned (85.7%). Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) and fuzzy set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) were combined. The study specific four-item benefit composite shows strong empirical coherence (Cronbach’s α = 0.936; McDonald’s ω = 0.937). CE-FDH NCA with 10,000 permutations identifies top management awareness as the only condition with both a practically meaningful and statistically supported necessity effect (d = 0.433, p < 0.001). Using frequency ≥ 2, consistency ≥ 0.80, and standard PRI ≥ 0.65, the observed-data complex fsQCA solution identifies two pathways: MGT*~TECH*~INTL*EXT and MGT*SIZE*INTL*EXT, with solution consistency 0.963 and coverage 0.595. A separate low outcome analysis yields different configurations, supporting causal asymmetry. Robustness checks show that management awareness is the most stable cross specification element, while exact pathway structure is sensitive to some coding and case-exclusion choices. The study contributes a transparent, bounded configurational explanation of e-logistics benefit realization in Bangladesh RMG.

papers.title: Simulated Light Schedules for Sleep-Wake Adjustments: Exploring the Incorporation of Reinforcement Learning

raw.title: Simulated Light Schedules for Sleep-Wake Adjustments: Exploring the Incorporation of Reinforcement Learning
raw.authorString: Seah M, Lim JMY, Liang S, Kumari Y, Kalavally V.
raw.abstractText: This study investigates the potential of a development framework for generating personalized light schedules aimed at achieving specific sleep-wake cycle targets. Unlike existing approaches that rely on predefined heuristics or static lighting recommendations, the framework formulates light scheduling as a sequential decision-making problem and employs a reinforcement learning–based deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm to iteratively modify real-world light exposure patterns toward achieving a desired sleep-wake class. This process is assisted by a convolutional neural network-based sleep-wake classification model trained on ecologically collected data. The circadian impacts of the generated schedules are evaluated using dim light melatonin onset (DLMO) simulations from a validated circadian model. By incorporating melanopic alongside photopic illuminances and embedding industry-oriented constraints, this work explores possibilities of a novel method in generating and modifying light schedules for sleep-wake adjustments using modern approaches, standards and findings.

papers.title: Spatial uncoupling of endothelial calcium signaling from phosphatidylserine externalization in vascular injury

raw.title: Spatial uncoupling of endothelial calcium signaling from phosphatidylserine externalization in vascular injury
raw.authorString: Fauver O, Hennig G, Sackheim A, Walters B, Barba R, Sonawane R, Bidlack C, Majumdar D, Trebak M, Nelson MT, Freeman K.
raw.abstractText: Ca2+ is both the signal that spreads injury information through the endothelium and the trigger for phospholipid scrambling that makes a membrane procoagulant. How a blood vessel can disseminate the first without broadcasting the second is unknown. Here, we combine single-cell laser injury in endothelial monolayers with imaging of intact mesenteric vessels in vitro and intravital Ca2+ imaging in vivo. Injury generated a coherent Ca2+ wavefront that spread rapidly before progressively slowing and terminating at a reproducible boundary 197 ± 7 μm from the wound, engaging 50 ± 8 cells. The first ring of neighboring cells exhibited a distinct response that was prevented by carbenoxolone, whereas propagation beyond this ring required extracellular ATP, purinergic receptor activation, and IP3-dependent Ca2+ release. Wavefront kinematics were consistent with ATP diffusion. In vivo, injury elicited vasoconstriction and bidirectional Ca2+ waves propagating 205 ± 28 μm before terminating. Remarkably, despite widespread Ca2+ elevations, phosphatidylserine (PS) externalization remained confined to the wounded cell in monolayers and intact vessels in vitro. In contrast, ionomycin-induced Ca2+ overload exposed phosphatidylserine in nearly all endothelial cells. These findings reveal an unexpected spatial uncoupling between endothelial Ca2+ signaling and phospholipid scrambling, demonstrating that Ca2+ dependent scramblase activation is subject to additional spatial regulation. The endothelium can therefore propagate injury signals across a broad field of cells while maintaining a highly localized procoagulant membrane response.

raw.abstractText: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is characterized by chronic hemolytic anemia and a propensity to acute exacerbations such as post-transfusion hyperhemolysis syndrome (HHS). While erythrocyte injury is secondary to hemoglobin S polymerization, the underlying pathophysiologic driver, the mechanism by which sickle erythrocytes are then removed from circulation is largely regulated by the immune system. Multiple pathways potentially play a role, driven by pathological changes within both the cellular and humoral immune system. The review examines what is known regarding changes to the outer membrane of the sickle erythrocyte (including the expression of phosphatidylserine (PS), mannose, CD47 and CD95/Fas), the role of plasma-derived opsonins (including Gas6, MFG-E8, Protein S, MBL, TSP1, IgG and C3b) and the macrophage receptors that recognize and bind these molecules (including TREM2, TIM4, MerTK, integrins αvβ3/5, CD206, CD209/DC-SIGN, SIRPα, FasL, FcR, and CR). Drawing upon the results of investigations by our group and others, we conclude with a proposed model for clearance of erythrocytes in SCD, in which chronic hemolysis predominantly occurs through extravascular erythrophagocytosis, whereas acute hemolytic events involve a shift towards intravascular hemolysis via complement assembly into the membrane attack complex, Fas-mediated erythronecroptosis, and heme-mediated ferroptosis. The process by which transfusion may accelerate these pathways and induce HHS is also considered.

raw.abstractText: Liver fibrosis is a severe complication of diverse chronic liver diseases characterized by a dysregulated hepatic microenvironment, and effective clinical therapeutic strategies for this condition remain lacking to date. Chimeric antigen receptor macrophages (CAR-Ms) hold considerable therapeutic potential for liver fibrosis via antigen-specific recognition and efferocytotic activity, yet their clinical translation is largely hindered by the sophisticated ex vivo preparation procedures. Herein, we report an in situ CAR-M engineering strategy that uses a phosphatidylserine (PS)-incorporated, macrophage-targeted lipid nanoparticle (LNP) for the codelivery of CAR messenger RNA (mRNA) and Cas9 mRNA in vivo. Our findings demonstrate that this engineered LNP achieves efficient targeting of liver-resident macrophages. Transfection with fibroblast activation protein α (FAPα)-CAR mRNA equips macrophages with the capacity to specifically target activated hepatic stellate cells (aHSCs), whereas Cas9-mediated follistatin-like protein 1 (FSTL-1) gene editing enhances the efferocytotic function of macrophages in liver tissues. Consequently, functional CAR-Ms are generated in situ, which elicits robust antifibrotic effects, including reduced collagen deposition, restored sinusoidal architecture and enhanced immune-mediated antifibrotic activity. Collectively, our customized LNP-mediated in situ engineering of liver macrophages into CAR-Ms enables precise antifibrotic intervention for liver fibrosis and circumvents the cumbersome ex vivo CAR-M preparation process.

raw.abstractText: Refractory chronic diabetic wounds severely impair quality of life. Their delayed healing is mainly driven by impaired angiogenesis and persistent inflammation caused by infection and excessive ROS. Resveratrol (RES) has anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic effects, but its clinical use is limited by poor solubility and low bioavailability. Here, we developed a dual-mechanism sustained-release system for RES to promote diabetic wound healing. RES was converted into nanoparticles (RES NPs) to improve cellular uptake and bioavailability, then encapsulated in GelMA cryogel microspheres (CMS) for injectable, sustained release. This system downregulated NF-κB signaling, reduced ROS, and suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines and COX2, thereby inhibiting arachidonic acid metabolism and promoting macrophage polarization from M1 to M2. Meanwhile, AMPK activation restored endothelial cell function, enhanced angiogenesis, and supported new vessel formation. Overall, this strategy accelerated high-quality wound repair in diabetic conditions.

raw.abstractText: Whether a decline in taurine drives aging is debated, and despite high millimolar intracellular concentrations, its function as a potential guardian of cytosolic homeostasis is unclear. Here, we show that aging increases circulating taurine concentrations in humans and mice. Further elevating taurine in aged mice enhances health span, engaging anti-inflammatory pathways previously linked to youthfulness, and reduces mortality from sepsis and inflammasome-mediated inflammation, suggesting an enantiostatic response. Mechanistically, diverse NLRP3-specific "danger signals" induce taurine efflux from macrophages as a proximal step to activate the inflammasome and the resultant pyroptosis. Taurine restoration in macrophages prevents NLRP3-induced trans-Golgi network disassembly, thereby suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Conversely, lowering taurine biosynthesis combined with reduced bioavailability in macrophages exacerbated inflammasome activation. In humans, sustained caloric restriction elevates adipose tissue taurine and is accompanied by lower inflammation. Together, we identify taurine as an immunometabolic rheostat that links danger sensing to NLRP3 inflammasome activation, suggesting taurine-based strategies to alleviate inflammaging and inflammasomopathies.

papers.title: LRRC8A/D-containing anion channels mediate swelling-activated taurine release in the mouse brain

raw.title: LRRC8A/D-containing anion channels mediate swelling-activated taurine release in the mouse brain
raw.authorString: Chandler ML, Nalwalk JW, Dohare P, Sprague AD, Schober AL, Mongin AA.
raw.abstractText: Volume-regulated anion channels (VRACs) are swelling-activated Cl⁻ channels formed by heteromers of LRRC8 proteins (LRRC8A-E). VRACs mediate regulatory volume decrease by releasing Cl⁻ and organic osmolytes, including taurine. In the brain, taurine functions as both an osmolyte and an inhibitory neuromodulator, acting as an agonist at glycine and GABAA receptors. Here, we used RNAi and genetically modified mice to (i) determine the contribution of LRRC8 subunits to swelling-activated taurine release, and (ii) test whether brain VRACs contribute to systemic osmoregulation. In astrocyte cultures lacking the essential VRAC subunit LRRC8A, swelling-activated [3H]taurine release was reduced by ~90%. Similarly, in vivo brain microdialysis revealed a ≥90% reduction in swelling-activated taurine release in brain-wide LRRC8A knockout mice (bLRRC8A KO). RNAi experiments further confirmed LRRC8D as a key determinant of VRAC-mediated taurine release, with Lrrc8d knockdown reducing swelling activated [3H]taurine efflux by >50%. RNA-seq revealed enrichment of Lrrc8d in the hypothalamus, where astrocytic taurine release is proposed to inhibit magnocellular neurons and suppress arginine vasopressin secretion during hypoosmotic conditions. We therefore tested whether disrupting brain VRACs impairs recovery from systemic hypoosmotic stress. bLRRC8A KO mice and mice with gene trap-mediated LRRC8D depletion were challenged with an intraperitoneal injection of sterile water (7.5% body weight, under anesthesia), and serum osmolality was monitored over time. Unexpectedly, neither model showed impaired recovery from hypoosmotic challenge. Overall, this study identifies LRRC8A/D-containing VRACs as the primary conduit for swelling-activated taurine release in the brain, yet indicates that this pathway is not essential for maintaining systemic fluid-electrolyte homeostasis.

raw.abstractText: Danshensu (DSS), a water-soluble bioactive compound with significant antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, cardioprotective and neuroprotective properties, is widely utilized in cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease. In this study, we established a multi-enzyme cascade system in engineered Escherichia coli to synthesize DSS from L-Tyrosine. The initial co-expression of 4-hydroxyphenylacetate 3-monooxygenase (HpaBC), L-amino acid deaminase (aadL), glucose dehydrogenase (gdh) and D-lactate dehydrogenase (ldhD) yielded 5.1 mM DSS. The production of DSS increased to 6.53 mM through optimizing plasmid copy number. After optimizing the conditions, the yield of DSS reached 8.66 mM from strain 6. Finally, whole cell biotransformation using strain 6 in bioreactor yielded 19.47 mM DSS within 32h. These findings provide valuable insights for the scalable biosynthesis of pharmaceutically important compound of DSS from naturally available substrates of L-Tyrosine.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Dopamine neurons in the ventral tegmental area (VTA), a midbrain structure, have been widely implicated in promoting emergence from general anesthesia. However, most studies have focused on anesthetics that primarily target γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptors. Whether these neurons also facilitate emergence from mechanistically diverse drug-induced unconscious states is not known. This study examined the specific contribution of VTA dopamine neurons in restoring arousal after sevoflurane-, dexmedetomidine-, fentanyl-, and ketamine-induced unconsciousness.

Methods

Adult Sprague Dawley rats received viral constructs driving selective expression in tyrosine hydroxylase-positive VTA neurons of either channelrhodopsin or the control protein, yellow fluorescent protein. Accurate targeting in VTA TH:ChR was confirmed by assessing righting in response to photostimulation during continuous sevoflurane inhalation (1.4 to 2.0%). In a randomized block design, the rats were exposed to dexmedetomidine (15 µg/kg IV bolus), fentanyl (50 µg/kg IV bolus), or ketamine (50 mg/kg IV infusion). After loss of the righting reflex, behavioral arousal and frontal electroencephalography activity were recorded with or without photostimulation. The proportion of animals righting during the light-on and light-off conditions was assessed in a mixed-effects Cox regression model, and spectral power differences were quantified with effect size estimates.

Results

Optogenetic stimulation of VTA dopamine neurons during continuous sevoflurane inhalation restored righting in VTA TH:ChR rats, with a median latency of 4.7 min (95% CI, 2.6 to 6.4) after the onset of photostimulation. VTA TH:ChR rats were significantly more likely to right during photostimulation after dexmedetomidine (hazard ratio, 27.7; 95% CI, 2.7 to 287.1; P = 0.0053), and responders showed attenuated spectral power in low frequencies (less than 12 Hz) in VTA TH:ChR . Optogenetic stimulation did not affect behavioral nor neurophysiologic measures of arousal after fentanyl. Finally, optogenetic stimulation in VTA TH:ChR rats modestly delayed emergence from ketamine sedation without altering electroencephalography spectral power.

Conclusions

These data suggest that the role of dopamine VTA neurons in anesthetic emergence is agent specific and likely shaped by distinct and sometimes opposing neural pathways.

payload.abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent the first line of host immune defense against a broad spectrum of microorganisms. Whether naturally occurring or synthetically designed, these small peptides can potently inhibit microbial growth and remain stable under diverse conditions. Most AMPs act by directly disrupting fungal or bacterial membranes. In this study, we identified a glycine-rich peptide with strong antifungal activity against Botrytis cinerea. We further investigated its mode of action (MOA) and demonstrated its preventive antifungal activity in plants. Our work focuses primarily on the in vitro characterization of AMP features in the context of plant-Botrytis interactions.

payload.title: Multienzyme cascade biotransformation of L-Tyrosine to Danshensu by engineered Escherichia coli
payload.abstract: Danshensu (DSS), a water-soluble bioactive compound with significant antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, cardioprotective and neuroprotective properties, is widely utilized in cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease. In this study, we established a multi-enzyme cascade system in engineered Escherichia coli to synthesize DSS from L-Tyrosine. The initial co-expression of 4-hydroxyphenylacetate 3-monooxygenase (HpaBC), L-amino acid deaminase (aadL), glucose dehydrogenase (gdh) and D-lactate dehydrogenase (ldhD) yielded 5.1 mM DSS. The production of DSS increased to 6.53 mM through optimizing plasmid copy number. After optimizing the conditions, the yield of DSS reached 8.66 mM from strain 6. Finally, whole cell biotransformation using strain 6 in bioreactor yielded 19.47 mM DSS within 32h. These findings provide valuable insights for the scalable biosynthesis of pharmaceutically important compound of DSS from naturally available substrates of L-Tyrosine.
